{{Navbar-GOGPT-tracker}}
'''Point Lisas power station''' is an operating power station of at least 812-megawatts (MW) in Point Lisas, Couva, Couva-Tabaquite-Talparo, Trinidad and Tobago.

==Background==

The first 88 MW gas-fired unit at Point Lisas was brought online in 1977. Two smaller units (20 MW each) were added in 1978, followed by three more 88 MW units and four 62.5 MW units between 1980 and 1982, and two 105 MW units in 2007.<ref name='ref_A'>{{cite web |url=https://www.powergen.co.tt/Locations/Point-Lisas-Power-Station |title=Point Lisas Power Station |date= |website=Powergen |access-date=May 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505203157/https://www.powergen.co.tt/Locations/Point-Lisas-Power-Station |archive-date=May 5, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Proposed changes to the Point Lisas plant include the replacement of older gas turbines with new turbines and the use of steam from the plant for power generation. However, these plans remain vague and there appears to be no fixed timeline for implementing them.<ref name='ref_A'>{{cite web |url=https://www.powergen.co.tt/Locations/Point-Lisas-Power-Station |title=Point Lisas Power Station |date= |website=Powergen |access-date=May 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505203157/https://www.powergen.co.tt/Locations/Point-Lisas-Power-Station |archive-date=May 5, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://energynow.tt/blog/powergen-upgrades-means-more-gas-for-energy|title=PowerGen upgrades means more gas for energy|last=|first=|date=March 10, 2017|website=Business Guardian|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>
